    • TOOL_PETRI_NET_SIM

      public static final String TOOL_PETRI_NET_SIM
      The identity of the web application that shares this PNML dialect.

      This project never writes a block under this name; only the web application does. It is kept here as the name a reader falls back to when an element carries none of TOOL_PETRI_OBJ_MODEL's own blocks, which is what lets a document the web application wrote open here without anything having to be converted on the way across.

      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • TOOL_VERSION_PETRI_OBJ_MODEL

      public static final String TOOL_VERSION_PETRI_OBJ_MODEL
      The release of this project that the TOOL_PETRI_OBJ_MODEL vocabulary belongs to, taken from this project's own pom.xml.

      It states a release, not a format revision, and no reader in this family filters on it; see TOOL_VERSION_OBJECT_MODEL_CONFORMANT. That is what makes it safe for the value to move with the project.

      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • TOOL_VERSION

      public static final String TOOL_VERSION
      The element-level version of the first format, stamped on the block of a place, a transition or an arc.

      Nothing writes it any more: the writers stamp TOOL_VERSION_PETRI_OBJ_MODEL on every block they produce. It sits in every file saved before that change, so it stays a value readers must accept.

      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • TOOL_VERSION_OBJECT_MODEL

      public static final String TOOL_VERSION_OBJECT_MODEL
      Tool-specific version of the first composed format, pages plus a positional link block, with no reference nodes.

      This project never wrote it, and no writer produces it now: the writers stamp TOOL_VERSION_PETRI_OBJ_MODEL. Other tools in this family did write it, and it is still sitting in saved files, so it stays a value readers must accept.

      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • TOOL_VERSION_OBJECT_MODEL_CONFORMANT

      public static final String TOOL_VERSION_OBJECT_MODEL_CONFORMANT
      Tool-specific version stamped on the page-level and net-level blocks of a document whose inter-object structure is also expressed with reference nodes.

      A version is a hint about what else the document carries, never a filter: a reader that selects tool-specific blocks by their version would drop the object metadata of every document written by a newer build. Match on ATTR_TOOL only.

      No writer stamps it any more: they state this project's release, TOOL_VERSION_PETRI_OBJ_MODEL. It stays here as a value readers must accept rather than one they may expect.

      See Also:

    • ELEMENT_PETRI_OBJECT_GROUPS

      public static final String ELEMENT_PETRI_OBJECT_GROUPS
      Net-level block recording which Petri-objects were stamped together as a group.

      Tool-specific because the PNML grammar has nothing to say about it and should not be asked to: a group is a statement about how a model was built, not about what it means. The objects it names are ordinary pages, related to each other by nothing but this block, so a reader that skips it reads the same model.

      See Also:

    • LINK_TYPE_PLACE_TO_TRANSITION

      public static final String LINK_TYPE_PLACE_TO_TRANSITION
      A retired link type, kept only so that a reader recognises it and can say why the document is refused. It made a place of one Petri-object an extra input of a transition of another, which gave that transition a second set of input places and so contradicted the definition of a Petri net transition. Nothing writes it any more, and a document that declares it is rejected rather than converted, because a silent conversion would change what the stored model says.
      See Also:

    • MAX_REFERENCE_DEPTH

      public static final int MAX_REFERENCE_DEPTH

    • ERROR_UNUSABLE_PAGE_INDEX

      public static final String ERROR_UNUSABLE_PAGE_INDEX
      Refuses a nested document whose pages do not state a usable object index. Document order is not object order once pages nest, and the links address objects by that index, so the order cannot be guessed from the document without re-binding every link.

    • WARNING_MALFORMED_POSITION

      public static final String WARNING_MALFORMED_POSITION
      A standard <graphics><position> attribute that did not parse as a number; %s = where, %s = which coordinate, %s = the text read. Unlike WARNING_MALFORMED_NUMBER this never says a default was used: the whole <position> is dropped instead, so a valid tool-specific <coordinates> is not shadowed by defaulting the corrupt half of a corrupt standard position to zero.
      See Also:
